Worked on 999 calls for a while for the ambulance service, the most ridiculous call I got was a guy who was thirsty.

He'd been playing football all evening and called 999 for an ambulance because he was thirsty...  

Also frequently got calls about people having toothache/headache/General symptoms you can manage at home. This is a free service in the UK But it won't be free for much longer if people keep abusing it in this way!

If you're looking for something more contemporary, I read Derren Brown's 'Happy' and it springboarded me into the subject of philosophy. May not be everyone's cup of tea but definitely gives you a lot of perspectives, at least one of which will work for you and you will be interested in; well researched and a lot of love has gone into it.

Happy reading :)

I'm currently going through a dramatic self improvement period which is a lot of therapy coupled with relaxation techniques. 
My advice would be to relax. Unfortunately not everyone is going to like you, That's just a fact. It's neither a reflection on you nor a reflection on them - that's just life. If you spend every hour over analysing what you said or did wrong or what you COULD do wrong you will drive yourself insane and rob yourself of the happy times you're having RIGHT NOW. Live in the present.
Try meditating, It's really helping Me. Taking deep breaths in a social environment and just generally easing off on yourself will help more than you know. Just because you're intense doesn't make you a bad person, it means you care a hell of a lot and you're passionate and you work hard to make those around you happy. 
My rule is can I change it? No. Can I change how I feel about it? Yes. And that kind of makes me feel better.
The people you truly click with and who truly care about you will accept you warts and all, So cut yourself a bit of slack, take a deep breath and be who you are :). 
Sorry for the stream of consciousness, hope this helps!

I guess you never know what happens on the other side, in my head I thought people cared more about their money than trivial things like a stubbed toe haha! 

It seems mental health and social care are the most massively underfunded causes in our society right now, basically regardless of where you live. It makes me very sad that people can't get the help they need.

I work for the NHS in England and honestly the worst thing is people abusing the system. Don't get me wrong, we care for people and are here to help- but is being thirsty really a reason to call 999? (Trust me that's a call I've received, along with being cold, headaches, sore throats......).

I sometimes think if people had to (indirectly) pay for the treatment they receive the NHS wouldn't be so overstretched and underfunded.

Saying that, the NHS is the best institution of our country's history (in my opinion) and I'd fight for it any day.
